newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain,China plan HK talks before handover--aide.
newsitem.headline: Britain,China plan HK talks before handover--aide.

text.p: British and Chinese leaders are likely to hold talks in Hong Kong hours before London hands the colony back to Beijing, a British official said on Thursday.
British Foreign Office spokesman in Hong Kong, Bill Dickson, said talks were being arranged but details of time, place and content had not been decided.
"There will be meetings obviously," he told Reuters in response to inquiries about local press reports predicting a British-Chinese summit. "But we haven't fixed anything yet."
China is sending President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen to a joint ceremony marking the end of 156 years of British rule over Hong Kong at midnight June 30.
Britain will be represented by heir to the throne Prince Charles, new Prime Minister Tony Blair and Foreign Secretary Robin Cook.
Hong Kong newspapers earlier reported that a Sino-British summit had been arranged hours before the handover.
An announcement on any such meeting, if it materialised, would be made "very much nearer the time", Dickson said.
Quarrels over democracy and human rights have marred the build-up to the change of flag.
But China has said it hopes for a fresh start in Sino-British ties under Blair, whose Labour Party routed the long-ruling Conservatives in elections last month.
